choices.why: Perfect of διερείδω, to prop up firmly.
Romans 8:11 as Cyril quotes it is in the second person.
Cyril mocks the endless 'How?' asked of God's works.

pass_a_gloss: [Continuing the previous section: the kingdom plundered of old and] having come to be under others, having restored (ἀποκαθίστημι) to him the holding of authority (κατεξουσιάζω) over all things on earth, death being abolished and Satan who had played the tyrant (τυραννέω) against them, the Son will have again also into the coming age the pre-eminence (ὑπεροχή) of authority over all things. [Heading] Tome Seven. [Lemma] But someone will say, How are the dead raised? And with what sort of body do they come? etc. The prophet Isaiah, with the [mystery] of the resurrection from the dead, had cried out beforehand (προανακράζω) the mystery, how it will be in due times, God nodding assent (κατανεύω) and by unspeakable power re-forming (μεταπλάσσω) into life what has been held by death, saying, 'The dead will stand up, and those in the tombs will be raised, and those in the earth will be made glad; for the dew from you is healing for them'; saying dew, I think, figuratively (τροπικῶς) for the life-making working of God, by which he both assigns (προσνέμω) being to things that are not, and grants well-being to things already brought into existence (ὕπαρξις); for all things stand together (συνίστημι) in him, just as of course also through him they were brought forth to coming-to-be. And the divine David sings somewhere about the things on earth, to the Saviour God of all: 'When you open your hand, all things together will be filled with goodness; when you turn away your face, they will be troubled; you will take away their spirit and they will fail, and to their dust they will return; you will send forth your spirit and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth.' For the nature of man suffered the turning away (ἀποστροφή) of the divine face in Adam through the transgression; accordingly it has been all but confounded (συγχέω) and troubled, and returned (ὑπονοστέω) to its own dust, and was brought down into death and corruption. But since the Only-begotten Word of God became according to us, and we have been enriched with the participation (μέθεξις) of the Holy Spirit, we are re-formed (ἀναμορφόω) to what was in the beginnings and as it were have been created again; for we have been called into newness of life, escaping (διαδιδράσκω) the might of death. And the most wise Paul will bear witness, saying, 'And if the spirit of the one who raised Jesus dwells in you, the one who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will make alive also your mortal bodies through his Spirit dwelling in you.' When then Christ lived again, treading the might of death, and became firstfruits of those fallen asleep, as [those who] will surely follow his tracks, how is it not utterly senseless (ἀπόπληκτος) to doubt (ἐνδοιάζω) still in any respect at all about the mystery of the resurrection? If someone should choose, putting in the eye of his own mind too curiously (περιεργότερον) on the works of the Godhead, to try to look around (περιαθρέω) at the manner of the bringing-forth (παραγωγή) of each and the beginning of its coming-to-be, he would never cease (καταλήγω) saying the senseless 'How?' For how did the heaven come to be, from what sort of matter or whence? What sort of seat does it have? And earth, how or whence, and where ever has it been made to rest firm (διερείδω)? And how was the circle of the sun brought forth, moon and stars and the other creatures? And how did the Maker (δημιουργός) of all, taking dust from earth, form man? How was the earth re-formed into bones and sinews and fleshes? And if, since we shall not be found [able] to give the account for each of the things made, in this way we shall also abolish that they came to be at all, where then would the outcome of the thoughts, or of perverse (σκαιός) attempts (ἐγχείρημα), finally end? To doubt (ἀμφιβάλλω) about resurrection after the resurrection of Christ is of ill counsel (δυσβουλία) and ignorance and boastfulness (ἀλαζονεία), to say the 'how' about the works of God; and indeed to say, With what sort of body are the dead raised, this too is simple-minded (εὐήθης); for it is very clear that [it is] with the same. For indeed the Lord too raised his own flesh as it was. And since some say that the soul pre-existed (προϋπάρχω), and is bound into (ἐνδεσμέω) the body for the sake of punishment, they set aside not only the account of creation according to which [continued in the next section].
pass_b_english: …restoring to him authority over all things on earth. When death and Satan, who had tyrannized over them, have been destroyed, the Son will again have, in the age to come as well, supremacy of authority over all things.

“But someone will say, ‘How are the dead raised? With what kind of body do they come?’” and so on (1 Corinthians 15:35). The prophet Isaiah cried out long beforehand the mystery of the resurrection from the dead, that it will take place in due time, as God grants it and by his unspeakable power refashions into life what death held fast. He said, “The dead shall rise, and those in the tombs shall be raised, and those in the earth shall rejoice; for the dew that comes from you is healing to them” (Isaiah 26:19). By dew, I think, he means figuratively the life-giving working of God, by which he gives being to things that are not, and grants well-being to things already brought into existence. For all things hold together in him (Colossians 1:17), just as they were also brought into being through him (compare John 1:3).

And somewhere the inspired David sings of the creatures on earth to God, the Savior of all: “When you open your hand, all things will be filled with goodness; when you turn away your face, they will be troubled; you will take away their spirit, and they will fail and return to their dust; you will send forth your Spirit, and they will be created, and you will renew the face of the earth” (Psalm 104:28–30). For in Adam, because of the transgression, human nature suffered the turning away of the divine face; and so it was all but thrown into confusion and troubled, went back to its own dust, and was brought down into death and corruption. But since the Only-begotten Word of God has become like us, and we have been enriched with a share in the Holy Spirit, we are being reshaped to what we were in the beginning and, as it were, created anew. For we have been called to newness of life (Romans 6:4), escaping the power of death.

The most wise Paul will bear witness, saying, “If the Spirit of him who raised Jesus dwells in you, he who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will give life to your mortal bodies also through his Spirit who dwells in you” (Romans 8:11). Since, then, Christ came to life again, trampling down the power of death, and became the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep, who will surely follow in his footsteps, how is it not utter madness still to doubt the mystery of the resurrection in any way at all?

If anyone chose to turn the eye of his mind too curiously on the works of the Godhead, and tried to look closely into the manner in which each thing was brought forth and the beginning of its coming to be, he would never stop uttering that senseless “How?” For how did the heaven come to be, from what matter, or from where? What foundation does it have? And the earth, how or from where did it come, and on what does it rest firm? How were the orb of the sun, the moon, the stars, and the other created things brought forth? How did the Maker of all take dust from the earth and form man (Genesis 2:7)? How was earth refashioned into bones and sinews and flesh? If, because we shall not be able to give an account of each thing that has been made, we shall for that reason deny that they came to be at all, where would these notions, or rather these perverse arguments, finally end?

After Christ’s resurrection, to doubt the resurrection, to say “How?” of the works of God, is a mark of bad judgment, ignorance, and arrogance. And indeed to ask, “With what body are the dead raised?” is also foolish; for it is quite plain that it is with the same body. For the Lord too raised his own flesh just as it was. But as for those who say that the soul existed beforehand and is bound to the body as a punishment, they set aside not only the account of creation, according to which…
